Keys joined with +, like "mod+shift+p". mod is ⌘ on Apple devices and Ctrl elsewhere. Names such as alt, enter, escape, up and space become symbols or short words, and get a spoken name for screen readers.

With `listen`, a cap presses down while its real key is held. It only watches, so it never blocks, delays or changes what you type. Letters match by physical key, so Option and Shift don't confuse them.
Write shortcuts once with `keys` and they show as ⌘K on a Mac and Ctrl K on Windows and Linux. Or pass any content as children for full control.
`keycap` has a hairline edge and a 1px lip so it reads as a physical key. `flat` is a quiet fill for dense places like menus.
`sm` sits in small text, `default` next to body text and `lg` in headings or on its own.
